 | WSV-07 | app ignores stop (slow-stop build), stop_timeout=10 | deploy succeeds; logs contain step FORCE_KILL; total STOP phase <25s |
 | WSV-08 | non-builtin account `.\svcuser` password_env | service ObjectName=.\svcuser; secret absent from `sc qc` capture in TF logs at TRACE |
 
 ### 18.6 NOD / NET
 
 | ID | When | Expected |
 |---|---|---|
 | NOD-01 | node app (bundled node_modules, install_deps=false), port 8087 | service running; `GET :8087/health` 200; env PORT visible in app.log |
 | NOD-02 | install_deps=true, artifact w/o package-lock.json | ERR_SERVICE_INSTALL mentioning lockfile; no service created (fresh) |
 | NOD-03 | install_deps=true with lockfile | `node_modules` exists in release dir; healthy |
 | NET-01 | dotnet self-contained, hosting native, urls :8088 | running; health ok; ASPNETCORE_URLS present in HKLM env |
 | NET-02 | launcher=dotnet_dll on box WITHOUT aspnet runtime | ERR_PREFLIGHT naming `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App` BEFORE any file copied |
 
 ### 18.7 CLU — failover cluster (C2 unless noted)
 
 | ID | When | Expected |
 |---|---|---|
 | CLU-01 | fresh apply v1.0.0 role `sample-role` | service exists on cn1+cn2 (start_type DEMAND); `Get-ClusterGroup sample-role` Online; owner ∈ {cn1,cn2}; health on owner ok; both manifests current=1.0.0; TF service_status=`online` |
 | CLU-02 | apply v1.1.0 while probe loop (1 Hz GET health via CAP) runs 120s | apply ok; probe outage ≤ drain-induced single gap ≤30s and only ONE gap; final owner = pre-update PASSIVE node; both nodes junction→1.1.0; role Online |
 | CLU-03 (C3) | apply v1.1.0 on 3 nodes | passives updated in hosts order (log order asserts); former owner updated last; exactly one MOVE_GROUP (plus optional preferred move) |
 | CLU-04 | apply v1.1.0 built `--health 500` | ERR_HEALTH_CHECK; role Online back on ORIGINAL owner; `/health` serves v=1.0.0; BOTH nodes junction→1.0.0; manifests last_operation=rolled_back; next plan shows pending change to 1.1.0 (desired ≠ actual) |
 | CLU-05 | block WinRM to cn2 mid-test (before apply) | apply ⇒ ERR_CONNECT host=cn2 during CONNECT/U0; cn1 untouched: junction & role owner unchanged, no partial switch |
 | CLU-06 | pre-create role `sample-role` bound to service `other-svc` | ERR_SERVICE_INSTALL conflict message includes both names; nothing modified |
 | CLU-07 | destroy purge | role absent, services deleted both nodes, `<root>\sample-svc` gone both nodes |
 | CLU-08 | preferred_owner=cn2, fresh+update | after each apply OwnerNode==cn2 |
 
 ### 18.8 RBK / DRF / DST / IDP / LCK
 
 | ID | When | Expected |
 |---|---|---|
 | RBK-01 | after WSV-02, apply `-var version=1.0.0` | success; FETCH log `cache_hit=true` (no network to artifact host — block it to prove); health v=1.0.0; previous_version=1.1.0 |
 | RBK-02 | keep_releases=1 (1.0.0 pruned), apply 1.0.0 | success WITH re-fetch (cache_hit=false) |
 | DRF-01 | Stop-Service manually; `terraform plan` | plan shows `service_status running→stopped`-driven update; apply performs Start ONLY (log: no FETCH/SWITCH steps) and converges |
 | DRF-02 | delete manifest.json; plan | plan = CREATE (state removed on refresh); apply reinstalls cleanly over leftovers (idempotent create must handle existing service ⇒ treats as update-config) |
 | DRF-03 | manually repoint junction to 1.0.0 while state says 1.1.0; plan | plan shows deployed_version drift; apply converges to 1.1.0 without artifact fetch |
 | DST-01 | destroy (purge) WSV deployment | service absent (`sc query`⇒1060), dir gone, state empty |
 | DST-02 | destroy_mode=abandon | no connection made (unroutable host would still succeed); state empty; machine untouched |
 | IDP-01 | re-apply identical spec (service running) | plan empty; with `-refresh-only` no changes; target file mtimes unchanged |
 | LCK-01 | start apply A (slow artifact); apply B parallel | B fails <5s ERR_LOCKED naming owner of A; A completes normally |
 | LCK-02 | plant `.lock` aged > lock_timeout; apply | success; WARN diag `stale lock … overridden` |
 
 ### 18.9 E2E — labdeploy_e2e_test resource
 
 | ID | When | Expected |
 |---|---|---|
 | E2E-01 | deploy 1.1.0 + TestRun vstest (all pass), triggers.run=1 | apply ok; outputs total=3 passed=3 failed=0 passed=true; `results_dir/results/*.trx` exists; `summary.json` matches; logs dir contains app.log copied from shared |
 | E2E-02 | FAIL_ONE=1, fail_on_test_failure=true | apply exit≠0 ERR_TEST_FAILED; **results_dir fully populated anyway**; no TF state for test resource (Create failed) — documented; deployment resource unaffected |
 | E2E-03 | same, fail_on_test_failure=false | apply ok; passed=false failed=1; pipeline gate demo uses output |
 | E2E-04 | runner.timeout_seconds=10 against sleep-forever test | ERR_TIMEOUT; on target the test process tree is DEAD (assert via process list); partial logs collected |
 | E2E-05 | collect.windows_event_logs provider filter | events json in logs dir; ONLY events ≥ test start time |
 | E2E-06 | triggers.run bumped 1→2, same everything | plan = replace; tests re-run |
 | E2E-07 | results.format none, exit-code-only runner exec | passed reflects exit code list; counters = -1 |
 
 ### 18.10 PIP — pipeline integration (smoke, uses W1)
 
 | ID | When | Expected |
 |---|---|---|
 | PIP-01 | GH workflow dispatch version=1.1.0 | green; uploaded artifact `e2e-results` contains trx+summary+logs; job summary echoes `summary` output |
 | PIP-02 | GH dispatch version=1.2.0-bad, auto_rollback=true rollback_to=1.1.0 | deploy job fails with ERR_SERVICE_START; rollback job runs, ends green; final target serves v=1.1.0 |
 | PIP-03 | ADO run of azure-pipelines.yml (pass case) | Tests tab shows 3 VSTest results; pipeline artifact `labdeploy-logs` present |
 
 Harness notes for the agent: drive these with terratest or shell+`terraform`
 against real VMs; W1/C2 provisioning scripts are out of scope of the provider
 repo but the matrix above is the acceptance gate. Scenario IDs MUST appear in
 test names 1:1.
 
 ---
 
 ## 19. Implementation Milestones (agent execution order)
 
 1. spec (types/parse/validate) + unit tests → 2. transport (local, ssh, winrm)
 → 3. artifact → 4. engine paths/manifest/lock/health with fake transport tests
 → 5. pattern windows_service + console → 6. deployment resource CRUD → run
 VAL/CON/ART/CAP/WSV → 7. node/dotnet → 8. cluster engine+pattern → CLU → 9.
 e2e_test resource + logs → E2E → 10. docker → 11. examples/pipelines → PIP →
 12. goreleaser packaging.
 
 ## 20. Build & Toolchain Constraints
 
 Go ≥1.22; deps pinned in go.mod: terraform-plugin-framework v1.x,
 terraform-plugin-log, masterzen/winrm, golang.org/x/crypto, pkg/sftp,
 gopkg.in/yaml.v3. `golangci-lint run` clean; `make build test`. Binary name
 `terraform-provider-labdeploy_v<version>`. No cgo. No external runner deps
 beyond terraform itself.
 
 ## 21. Decision Table (ambiguity killers — binding)
 
 | # | Question | Decision |
 |---|---|---|
 | D1 | "provider deployed to target machine"? | Provider always runs on runner; runner==target supported via `transport: local`. |
 | D2 | How are non-SCM exes (node, plain console) run as services? | WinSW; wrapper binary MUST ship inside the artifact (`winsw_exe`). Provider never downloads third-party binaries. |
 | D3 | nupkg semantics | Unzip-in-place; no NuGet client on target. Version/dir name from spec, not nuspec. |
 | D4 | Health check origin | Always executed ON the target (localhost reachable, firewall-independent). |
 | D5 | Cluster binary placement | Local disk per node, identical paths. CSV = v2. |
 | D5b | Cluster + wrapper | Not supported v1; exe must be SCM-aware. |
 | D6 | Secrets | Env-var-name indirection everywhere; values never persisted (§11). |
 | D7 | YAML vs JSON precedence | Both accepted; canonical JSON drives hashing/plan. |
 | D8 | Downgrade | Same code path as upgrade + release cache reuse (§10.3). |
 | D9 | Import | Unsupported v1 (clear error). |
 | D10 | PowerShell baseline | Windows PowerShell 5.1 (no pwsh7 dependency). |
 | D11 | Update failing mid-way, rollback ok | TF state keeps old version; machine restored to old ⇒ consistent by construction. |
 | D12 | Who prunes releases | Engine, after successful FINALIZE only; never deletes `previous_version`. |
 | D13 | E2E on failure leaves no state | Accepted; `triggers` replace-model makes re-runs cheap; reporting mode via `fail_on_test_failure=false`. |
 | D14 | Docker on Windows | Supported when `docker version` preflight passes; otherwise ERR_PREFLIGHT. |
 | D15 | Where do E2E artifacts land in pipelines | Always under `collect.destination_dir`; pipelines publish with always()/condition:always. |

1. @story-release:RELEASE-PROVIDER @phase-terraform-provider-surface @stage-deployment-resource-crud-and-plan-modifiers @setup-inline
2. Feature: Deployment resource CRUD and plan modifiers
3.   The labdeploy_deployment resource forces replacement on immutable spec paths,
4.   treats host reordering as a no-op, surfaces coded diagnostics, computes a
5.   deterministic host-order-independent id, applies timeout defaults, and refuses
6.   import (DESIGN §5.2, §12).
7. 
8.   Scenario Outline: RequiresReplace fires on immutable path <field>
9.     Given a prior deployment snapshot in state
10.     And a plan that changes only the immutable field "<field>"
11.     When the deployment plan is computed
12.     Then the change forces RequiresReplace
13. 
14.     Examples:
15.       | field        |
16.       | pattern.type |
17.       | service_name |
18.       | target.hosts |
19.       | target.os    |
20. 
21.   Scenario: Host reorder is not a replacement
22.     Given a prior deployment snapshot with hosts "lab-01,lab-02"
23.     And a plan with the same hosts reordered to "lab-02,lab-01" and no other change
24.     When the deployment plan is computed
25.     Then RequiresReplace does not fire
26. 
27.   Scenario: Create surfaces a coded ERR_CONNECT diagnostic Summary
28.     Given a deployment whose engine preflight fails with the ERR_CONNECT taxonomy code
29.     When Create surfaces the failure
30.     Then the diagnostic Summary begins with "[ERR_CONNECT] "
31. 
32.   Scenario: Deterministic host-order-independent SHA-1 id
33.     Given a spec with name "n" and hosts "b,a"
34.     When the deployment id is computed
35.     Then it equals the sha1(sorted(hosts)+"/"+name)[0:12] + ":" + name formula
36.     And it is byte-identical when the same hosts are supplied in a different order
37. 
38.   Scenario: Timeout defaults when none are configured
39.     Given a deployment resource config with no explicit timeouts
40.     When the resource timeout defaults are read
41.     Then create and update default to 30m and delete defaults to 15m
42. 
43.   Scenario: Import is unsupported
44.     Given the labdeploy_deployment resource
45.     When terraform import is invoked on it
46.     Then the error is "import is not supported; adopt via apply"
47.

1. package provider
2. 
3. import (
4. 	"context"
5. 	"crypto/sha1"
6. 	"encoding/hex"
7. 	"encoding/json"
8. 	"errors"
9. 	"fmt"

15. 
16. 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework-timeouts/resource/timeouts"
17. 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework/diag"
18. 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework/path"
19. 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework/resource"
20. 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework/resource/schema"
21. 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework/resource/schema/planmodifier"
22. 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework/resource/schema/stringdefault"
23. 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework/resource/schema/stringplanmodifier"
24. 	"github.com/hashicorp/terraform-plugin-framework/types"
25. 
26. 	"github.com/smartpcr/terraform-provider-labdeploy/internal/engine"
27. 	"github.com/smartpcr/terraform-provider-labdeploy/internal/spec"
28. )
29. 
30. // Timeout defaults for the deployment lifecycle (DESIGN §5.2): create/update run
31. // long-lived deploys (30m); destroy is bounded tighter (15m).
32. const (
33. 	defaultCreateTimeout = 30 * time.Minute
34. 	defaultUpdateTimeout = 30 * time.Minute
35. 	defaultDeleteTimeout = 15 * time.Minute
36. )
37. 
38. var (
39. 	_ resource.Resource                     = (*DeploymentResource)(nil)
40. 	_ resource.ResourceWithConfigure        = (*DeploymentResource)(nil)
41. 	_ resource.ResourceWithModifyPlan       = (*DeploymentResource)(nil)
42. 	_ resource.ResourceWithImportState      = (*DeploymentResource)(nil)
43. 	_ resource.ResourceWithConfigValidators = (*DeploymentResource)(nil)
44. 	_ resource.ResourceWithUpgradeState     = (*DeploymentResource)(nil)
45. )
46. 
47. func NewDeploymentResource() resource.Resource { return &DeploymentResource{} }
48. 
49. type DeploymentResource struct {
50. 	pd *providerData
51. 	// newEngine is an OPTIONAL test seam (DESIGN §17): when nil the resource uses
52. 	// the real engine.New(); unit tests inject a fake so a lifecycle path (e.g. the
53. 	// state-rm + apply recovery Create) can be exercised end-to-end without a live
54. 	// transport. Production always leaves it nil.
55. 	newEngine func() deployEngine
56. }
57. 
58. // deployEngine is the narrow engine surface the resource depends on. It exists so
59. // tests can inject a fake at the engine boundary (DESIGN §17) rather than
60. // reimplementing the transport-script protocol. realEngine adapts *engine.Engine.
61. type deployEngine interface {
62. 	Update(ctx context.Context, s, prior *spec.Deployment) (*engine.Status, error)
63. 	ReadStatus(ctx context.Context, s *spec.Deployment) (*engine.Status, error)
64. 	Destroy(ctx context.Context, s *spec.Deployment, mode string) error
65. 	Warns() []string
66. }
67. 
68. type realEngine struct{ *engine.Engine }
69. 
70. func (r realEngine) Warns() []string { return r.Engine.Warnings }
71. 
72. func (r *DeploymentResource) engine() deployEngine {
73. 	if r.newEngine != nil {
74. 		return r.newEngine()
75. 	}
76. 	return realEngine{engine.New()}
77. }
78. 
79. // ConfigValidators enforces the VAL-06 exactly-one-of(spec, spec_file) rule at
80. // the Terraform config layer (DESIGN §14).
81. func (r *DeploymentResource) ConfigValidators(_ context.Context) []resource.ConfigValidator {
82. 	return []resource.ConfigValidator{exactlyOneOfSpecValidator{}}
83. }
84. 
85. type deploymentModel struct {
86. 	ID              types.String   `tfsdk:"id"`
87. 	Name            types.String   `tfsdk:"name"`
88. 	Spec            types.String   `tfsdk:"spec"`
89. 	SpecFile        types.String   `tfsdk:"spec_file"`
90. 	Variables       types.Map      `tfsdk:"variables"`
91. 	VersionOverride types.String   `tfsdk:"version_override"`
92. 	DestroyMode     types.String   `tfsdk:"destroy_mode"`
93. 	SpecHash        types.String   `tfsdk:"spec_hash"`
94. 	ResolvedSpec    types.String   `tfsdk:"resolved_spec"`
95. 	DeployedVersion types.String   `tfsdk:"deployed_version"`
96. 	PreviousVersion types.String   `tfsdk:"previous_version"`
97. 	Hosts           types.List     `tfsdk:"hosts"`
98. 	ReleasePath     types.String   `tfsdk:"release_path"`
99. 	ServiceStatus   types.String   `tfsdk:"service_status"`
100. 	Timeouts        timeouts.Value `tfsdk:"timeouts"`
101. }
102. 
103. func (r *DeploymentResource) Metadata(_ context.Context, req resource.MetadataRequest, resp *resource.MetadataResponse) {
104. 	resp.TypeName = req.ProviderTypeName + "_deployment"
105. }
106. 
107. func (r *DeploymentResource) Schema(ctx context.Context, _ resource.SchemaRequest, resp *resource.SchemaResponse) {
108. 	resp.Schema = deploymentSchema(ctx, 1)
109. }
110. 
111. // deploymentSchema builds the resource schema at the given version. The attribute
112. // shape is identical across versions — only Version differs — so the same builder
113. // serves both the current Schema (v1) and the UpgradeState PriorSchema (v0). The v0→v1
114. // bump exists solely to trigger the state upgrader that backfills resolved_spec for
115. // legacy state persisted before the snapshot was populated.
116. func deploymentSchema(ctx context.Context, version int64) schema.Schema {
117. 	return schema.Schema{
118. 		Version:             version,

155. // UpgradeState migrates state persisted at an earlier schema version. The v0→v1
156. // upgrader BACKFILLS resolved_spec for legacy state written before the snapshot
157. // attribute was populated, converting an unverifiable spec_file deployment into a
158. // VERIFIED snapshot BEFORE any plan/refresh acts on it. This is the migration path
159. // that breaks the legacy deadlock (ModifyPlan forcing replacement ↔ Delete refusing
160. // snapshot-less state) WITHOUT any unsafe deletion.
161. //
162. // The backfill is TRUSTWORTHY ONLY when the current spec_file still resolves to the
163. // SAME spec_hash that was persisted at the last apply — i.e. the file has NOT been
164. // edited since the deployment. If the operator upgraded the provider AND edited the
165. // spec in the same step, the file now describes the DESIRED (not deployed) config, so
166. // snapshotting it would fabricate a false prior — suppressing immutable replacement,
167. // reconfiguration, changed post_install, and truthful rollback. In that case (or when
168. // no baseline spec_hash exists, or the spec cannot be resolved) we DECLINE to backfill,
169. // leave resolved_spec empty, warn, and let the downstream Read/Delete guards +
170. // legacyReplaceRequired safeguard keep the state fail-safe.
171. func (r *DeploymentResource) UpgradeState(ctx context.Context) map[int64]resource.StateUpgrader {
172. 	priorSchema := deploymentSchema(ctx, 0)
173. 	return map[int64]resource.StateUpgrader{
174. 		0: {
175. 			PriorSchema: &priorSchema,
176. 			StateUpgrader: func(ctx context.Context, req resource.UpgradeStateRequest, resp *resource.UpgradeStateResponse) {
177. 				var state deploymentModel
178. 				resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &state)...)
179. 				if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
180. 					return
181. 				}
182. 				if state.ResolvedSpec.IsNull() || state.ResolvedSpec.ValueString() == "" {
183. 					r.backfillResolvedSpec(ctx, &state, &resp.Diagnostics)
184. 				}
185. 				resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, &state)...)
186. 			},
187. 		},
188. 	}
189. }
190. 
191. // backfillResolvedSpec reconstructs the resolved_spec snapshot for legacy state, but
192. // ONLY when the current spec resolves to the persisted spec_hash (proving the source
193. // is unchanged since deployment, so the snapshot faithfully captures the DEPLOYED
194. // identity). A missing baseline hash, a hash mismatch (source edited), a resolve
195. // error, or a provider default_target that contributes merged fields the pre-merge
196. // hash never covered all cause it to DECLINE and warn — never fabricate a prior.
197. func (r *DeploymentResource) backfillResolvedSpec(ctx context.Context, state *deploymentModel, diags *diag.Diagnostics) {
198. 	d, hash, defaultsContributed, err := r.resolveSpecDetail(ctx, state)
199. 	if err != nil {
200. 		diags.AddWarning("[WARN] labdeploy state not fully migrated",
201. 			"could not reconstruct a resolved_spec snapshot for this legacy resource "+
202. 				"(the spec could not be resolved: "+err.Error()+"). Lifecycle operations "+
203. 				"remain fail-safe; run terraform apply once the spec is resolvable to persist "+
204. 				"the snapshot.")
205. 		return
206. 	}
207. 	persisted := state.SpecHash.ValueString()
208. 	if persisted == "" || persisted != hash {
209. 		// The source no longer matches what was deployed (edited alongside the provider
210. 		// upgrade) or there is no baseline to compare. Snapshotting now would record the
211. 		// DESIRED config as the deployed prior — a false, high-impact fabrication. Decline.
212. 		diags.AddWarning("[WARN] labdeploy state not fully migrated",
213. 			"the current spec no longer matches the spec_hash recorded at the last apply "+
214. 				"(or no baseline spec_hash exists), so a resolved_spec snapshot cannot be "+
215. 				"trusted to reflect the DEPLOYED configuration. Leaving the snapshot unset so "+
216. 				"immutable-field replacement, reconfiguration, and rollback stay truthful; "+
217. 				"re-apply against the currently deployed spec to persist a faithful snapshot.")
218. 		return
219. 	}
220. 	if defaultsContributed {
221. 		// spec_hash matches because it is computed over the RAW spec, BEFORE provider
222. 		// default_target is merged. A default_target that now contributes target fields
223. 		// (transport/os/port/credentials/winrm) means the resolved_spec identity depends
224. 		// on provider config the persisted hash never covered — the merged fields may
225. 		// never have been deployed. Decline so a provider-default change cannot fabricate
226. 		// the deployed identity during state migration.
227. 		diags.AddWarning("[WARN] labdeploy state not fully migrated",
228. 			"the current spec relies on provider default_target values to fill one or more "+
229. 				"target fields, but spec_hash is computed before those defaults are merged, "+
230. 				"so it cannot prove the merged configuration was ever deployed. Leaving the "+
231. 				"resolved_spec snapshot unset so immutable-field replacement, reconfiguration, "+
232. 				"and rollback stay truthful; re-apply against the currently deployed spec to "+
233. 				"persist a faithful snapshot.")
234. 		return
235. 	}
236. 	state.ResolvedSpec = marshalResolvedSpec(d)
237. }

246. // resolveSpec loads+parses the deployment for a model (DESIGN §6.1).
247. func (r *DeploymentResource) resolveSpec(ctx context.Context, m *deploymentModel) (*spec.Deployment, string, error) {
248. 	d, hash, _, err := r.resolveSpecDetail(ctx, m)
249. 	return d, hash, err
250. }

252. // resolveSpecDetail is resolveSpec plus a defaultsContributed flag reporting whether
253. // the provider's default_target actually filled any target field during the merge.
254. // spec_hash is computed over the RAW (pre-merge) spec, so it CANNOT detect a change to
255. // provider default_target: an unchanged spec_file hashes identically even when a new
256. // default now contributes never-deployed fields to the resolved spec. The flag lets the
257. // state-migration backfill refuse to snapshot a resolved_spec whose identity depends on
258. // provider config that the persisted hash never covered.
259. func (r *DeploymentResource) resolveSpecDetail(ctx context.Context, m *deploymentModel) (*spec.Deployment, string, bool, error) {
260. 	hasSpec := !m.Spec.IsNull() && m.Spec.ValueString() != ""
261. 	hasFile := !m.SpecFile.IsNull() && m.SpecFile.ValueString() != ""
262. 	if hasSpec == hasFile {
263. 		return nil, "", false, fmt.Errorf("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] exactly one of spec/spec_file must be set")
264. 	}
265. 	raw := m.Spec.ValueString()
266. 	if hasFile {
267. 		b, err := os.ReadFile(m.SpecFile.ValueString())
268. 		if err != nil {
269. 			return nil, "", false, fmt.Errorf("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] spec_file: %w", err)
270. 		}
271. 		raw = string(b)
272. 	}
273. 	vars := map[string]string{}
274. 	if !m.Variables.IsNull() {
275. 		if diag := m.Variables.ElementsAs(ctx, &vars, false); diag.HasError() {
276. 			return nil, "", false, fmt.Errorf("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] variables: %v", diag.Errors())
277. 		}
278. 	}
279. 	d, hash, err := spec.ParseDeploymentLenient(raw, vars, m.VersionOverride.ValueString())
280. 	if err != nil {
281. 		return nil, "", false, err // already [ERR_SPEC_INVALID]-coded by the spec package
282. 	}
283. 	defaultsContributed := false
284. 	if r.pd != nil && r.pd.DefaultTarget != nil {
285. 		before := d.Target
286. 		spec.MergeTargetDefaults(&d.Target, r.pd.DefaultTarget)
287. 		defaultsContributed = !reflect.DeepEqual(before, d.Target)
288. 	}
289. 	if err := spec.ValidateDeployment(d); err != nil { // validate post-merge (DESIGN §6.2)
290. 		return nil, "", false, err // already [ERR_SPEC_INVALID]-coded
291. 	}
292. 	return d, hash, defaultsContributed, nil
293. }

295. // immutableKey captures the spec paths that force replacement (DESIGN §5.2):
296. // pattern.type, service_name, role_name, install_root, metadata.name,
297. // target.hosts, target.os. target.hosts is compared as a SET (lower-cased and
298. // sorted) per architecture.md line 350: reordering the same hosts is NOT a
299. // replacement, only adding/removing a host is.
300. func immutableKey(d *spec.Deployment) string {
301. 	hosts := make([]string, len(d.Target.Hosts))
302. 	for i, h := range d.Target.Hosts {
303. 		hosts[i] = strings.ToLower(h)
304. 	}
305. 	sort.Strings(hosts)
306. 	return strings.Join([]string{
307. 		string(d.Pattern.Type), d.Pattern.ServiceName, d.Pattern.RoleName,
308. 		d.Pattern.EffectiveInstallRoot(d.Target.OS), d.Metadata.Name,
309. 		strings.Join(hosts, ","), string(d.Target.OS),
310. 	}, "|")
311. }

313. // Recovery procedures surfaced in migration/corruption diagnostics. These are
314. // EXECUTABLE and reach VERIFIED state without the dead-ends the guards block: neither
315. // `terraform apply -replace` (whose Delete half is refused for unverifiable/corrupt
316. // state) nor "pin the defaulted fields then apply" (which changes the pre-merge hash and
317. // so forces the same blocked replacement). The escape hatch is `terraform state rm`
318. // followed by `terraform apply`: state rm is a state-only operation (it never touches the
319. // live service or invokes Delete), and the subsequent apply recreates the resource via
320. // Create, which deploys IDEMPOTENTLY (adopting the already-running service when the spec
321. // matches it) and persists a verified resolved_spec snapshot. ModifyPlan's create branch
322. // returns before the update guards, so this path is never blocked.
323. const (
324. 	// recoveryUnverifiableDefaults applies when the deployed identity cannot be verified
325. 	// from state AND provider default_target contributes immutable fields the pre-merge
326. 	// spec_hash does not cover.
327. 	recoveryUnverifiableDefaults = "the deployed identity cannot be verified from state and " +
328. 		"the provider default_target contributes one or more target fields (transport/os/port/" +
329. 		"hosts/credentials/winrm) that spec_hash — computed before defaults are merged — does not " +
330. 		"cover, so planning an update could deploy to a newly-defaulted target and orphan the " +
331. 		"original deployment. Recovery: first make this spec (or default_target) describe the " +
332. 		"ACTUALLY deployed identity, then run `terraform state rm <address>` followed by " +
333. 		"`terraform apply`. state rm is state-only (it never destroys the live service or invokes " +
334. 		"the guarded Delete); the apply then recreates via Create, which deploys idempotently " +
335. 		"(adopting the existing service when the spec matches) and persists a verified resolved_spec " +
336. 		"snapshot. Do NOT instead pin the defaults and re-apply in place: that changes the pre-merge " +
337. 		"hash and forces a replacement whose Delete half is refused for this unverifiable state."
338. 
339. 	// recoveryUnverifiableLegacy applies to legacy spec_file state with no snapshot and no
340. 	// contributing defaults.
341. 	recoveryUnverifiableLegacy = "this resource predates resolved_spec and is configured via " +
342. 		"spec_file, so its deployed identity cannot be verified from state. Recovery: run " +
343. 		"`terraform apply` WITHOUT editing the spec_file — with no immutable change pending, planning " +
344. 		"does not force a replacement, so the apply flows through Update and persists a resolved_spec " +
345. 		"snapshot from the currently-deployed spec. If planning instead forces a replacement (e.g. the " +
346. 		"spec must change), run `terraform state rm <address>` then `terraform apply` to re-adopt via a " +
347. 		"fresh Create. Both reach verified state without the guarded Delete destroying an unverifiable " +
348. 		"identity. (Do NOT use `terraform apply -replace` — its destroy half is blocked for exactly " +
349. 		"this reason.)"
350. 
351. 	// recoveryCorruptSnapshot applies when a non-empty resolved_spec cannot be decoded. It
352. 	// cannot be repaired in place; the state entry must be removed so the resource can be
353. 	// re-adopted against the live service.
354. 	recoveryCorruptSnapshot = "the persisted resolved_spec snapshot is corrupt and cannot be " +
355. 		"decoded, so the deployed identity is unknown; the Read/Delete guards refuse to act on it to " +
356. 		"avoid querying or destroying the wrong identity. Recovery: run `terraform state rm <address>` " +
357. 		"then `terraform apply` to re-adopt via a fresh Create (which deploys idempotently and persists " +
358. 		"a verified snapshot), or restore a known-good state backup — the corrupt snapshot cannot be " +
359. 		"repaired in place, and state rm never invokes the guarded Delete."
360. )

362. // ModifyPlan computes spec_hash drift and RequiresReplace on immutable paths.
363. func (r *DeploymentResource) ModifyPlan(ctx context.Context, req resource.ModifyPlanRequest, resp *resource.ModifyPlanResponse) {
364. 	if req.Plan.Raw.IsNull() { // destroy
365. 		return
366. 	}
367. 	var plan deploymentModel
368. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.Plan.Get(ctx, &plan)...)
369. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
370. 		return
371. 	}
372. 	newSpec, newHash, defaultsContributed, err := r.resolveSpecDetail(ctx, &plan)
373. 	if err != nil {
374. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_SPEC_INVALID", "invalid spec", err), err.Error())
375. 		return
376. 	}
377. 	plan.SpecHash = types.StringValue(newHash)
378. 	// Persist the fully-resolved spec at plan time so it is known (no perpetual
379. 	// "known after apply" diff) and so a later Update can compare against it even
380. 	// after spec_file contents change on disk.
381. 	plan.ResolvedSpec = marshalResolvedSpec(newSpec)
382. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.Plan.Set(ctx, &plan)...)
383. 
384. 	if req.State.Raw.IsNull() { // create
385. 		return
386. 	}
387. 	var state deploymentModel
388. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &state)...)
389. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
390. 		return
391. 	}
392. 	// Compare against the PERSISTED prior spec, not a fresh re-read of spec_file
393. 	// (which by plan time already holds the NEW contents and would make old == new,
394. 	// hiding immutable-field changes).
395. 	oldSpec, perr := r.priorFromState(ctx, &state)
396. 	if perr != nil {
397. 		// Corrupt persisted snapshot: fail loudly (consistent with stateSpec) rather than
398. 		// planning an update against an untrustworthy prior that could target the wrong host.
399. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_SPEC_INVALID", "invalid spec in state", perr), perr.Error())
400. 		return
401. 	}
402. 	if oldSpec == nil {
403. 		// No faithful prior snapshot. When provider default_target contributes fields to the
404. 		// resolved spec, spec_hash (computed pre-merge) cannot detect a default change, and
405. 		// because that hash is unchanged we CANNOT hang a replacement off spec_hash. Adopting
406. 		// the merged spec would silently deploy to the newly-defaulted target and orphan the
407. 		// original deployment. BLOCK the plan with an executable recovery instead of laundering
408. 		// the unverifiable merged identity into state.
409. 		if defaultsContributed {
410. 			resp.Diagnostics.AddError("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] labdeploy state migration required", recoveryUnverifiableDefaults)
411. 			return
412. 		}
413. 		// Otherwise the v0→v1 state upgrader normally backfilled resolved_spec already; this
414. 		// branch is only reached when even the upgrader could not reconstruct a snapshot. We
415. 		// cannot honestly Reconfigure without the ACTUAL prior configuration, so when the
416. 		// resolved spec really changed (hash drift), force a REPLACEMENT to apply the change via
417. 		// a full, truthful create/deploy. No drift ⇒ nothing to do.
418. 		if legacyReplaceRequired(oldSpec, newHash, &state) {
419. 			resp.RequiresReplace = append(resp.RequiresReplace, path.Root("spec_hash"))
420. 		}
421. 		return
422. 	}
423. 	if immutableKey(oldSpec) != immutableKey(newSpec) {
424. 		resp.RequiresReplace = append(resp.RequiresReplace, configuredSpecPath(&plan))
425. 	}
426. }
427. 
428. // legacyReplaceRequired reports whether an update must be handled as a truthful
429. // REPLACEMENT because no faithful prior snapshot exists to reconfigure against.
430. // oldSpec==nil means priorFromState could not reconstruct a trustworthy prior
431. // (legacy spec_file state written before resolved_spec); newHash != the persisted
432. // spec_hash means the resolved spec really changed. When both hold, forcing a
433. // replacement is safer than feeding fabricated prior state to Reconfigure. No drift
434. // ⇒ no change to apply, so no replacement.
435. func legacyReplaceRequired(oldSpec *spec.Deployment, newHash string, state *deploymentModel) bool {
436. 	return oldSpec == nil && newHash != state.SpecHash.ValueString()
437. }
438. 
439. // configuredSpecPath returns the schema path of whichever spec attribute the
440. // configuration actually sets, so a forced replacement is attributed to spec_file
441. // when that is the source rather than always to spec.
442. func configuredSpecPath(m *deploymentModel) path.Path {
443. 	if !m.SpecFile.IsNull() && m.SpecFile.ValueString() != "" {
444. 		return path.Root("spec_file")
445. 	}
446. 	return path.Root("spec")
447. }

449. // marshalResolvedSpec serializes a resolved deployment to canonical JSON for
450. // persistence in the resolved_spec computed attribute. password_env and other
451. // secret references are stored by NAME, but ${var:...} substitutions may embed
452. // secret values into other fields, so the snapshot can contain sensitive data —
453. // it is persisted only in the Sensitive resolved_spec attribute. Returns null on
454. // the (practically impossible) marshal error.
455. func marshalResolvedSpec(d *spec.Deployment) types.String {
456. 	b, err := json.Marshal(d)
457. 	if err != nil {
458. 		return types.StringNull()
459. 	}
460. 	return types.StringValue(string(b))
461. }

481. func (r *DeploymentResource) Update(ctx context.Context, req resource.UpdateRequest, resp *resource.UpdateResponse) {
482. 	var plan deploymentModel
483. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.Plan.Get(ctx, &plan)...)
484. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
485. 		return
486. 	}
487. 	updateTimeout, diags := plan.Timeouts.Update(ctx, defaultUpdateTimeout)
488. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(diags...)
489. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
490. 		return
491. 	}
492. 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, updateTimeout)
493. 	defer cancel()
494. 	// Resolve the PRIOR spec from state so a same-artifact configuration change is
495. 	// routed through the transactional Reconfigure path instead of Deploy, whose
496. 	// idempotency short-circuit would otherwise skip it. Decoding errors are NOT
497. 	// swallowed — corrupt/incompatible state must surface rather than silently
498. 	// downgrade to a blind Deploy.
499. 	var state deploymentModel
500. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &state)...)
501. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
502. 		return
503. 	}
504. 	prior, perr := r.priorFromState(ctx, &state)
505. 	if perr != nil {
506. 		// Corrupt persisted snapshot: surface it (consistent with stateSpec / ModifyPlan)
507. 		// rather than feeding a fabricated or nil prior into a blind Deploy.
508. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_SPEC_INVALID", "invalid spec in state", perr), perr.Error())
509. 		return
510. 	}
511. 	r.apply(ctx, &plan, prior, &resp.Diagnostics, func(m *deploymentModel) {
512. 		resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, m)...)
513. 	})
514. }

516. // priorFromState reconstructs the prior deployment from the PERSISTED resolved_spec
517. // (written verbatim on the last apply/plan), so it is faithful regardless of whether
518. // the prior spec came from inline `spec` or from a `spec_file` whose contents have
519. // since changed on the runner. This is what lets a same-artifact spec_file
520. // configuration change route correctly through Reconfigure (applying CONFIGURE and a
521. // changed post_install) while a real artifact upgrade still routes to Deploy, and it
522. // gives rollback the ACTUAL prior configuration to restore. A non-empty resolved_spec
523. // that fails to decode is STATE CORRUPTION: it returns an error (consistent with
524. // stateSpec) so Update/ModifyPlan fail loudly instead of fabricating a prior. Falls back
525. // to re-parsing inline spec for state written before resolved_spec existed (still faithful
526. // verbatim); returns (nil, nil) for legacy spec_file state (whose on-disk contents cannot
527. // be trusted as the prior) so ModifyPlan can force a truthful replacement.
528. func (r *DeploymentResource) priorFromState(ctx context.Context, state *deploymentModel) (*spec.Deployment, error) {
529. 	if rs := state.ResolvedSpec.ValueString(); rs != "" {
530. 		var d spec.Deployment
531. 		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(rs), &d); err != nil {
532. 			// Corrupt snapshot: do NOT fall back to the mutable spec_file (which could target
533. 			// the wrong identity) and do NOT return a nil "no prior" (which Update would treat
534. 			// as a blind first deploy). Surface it as state corruption.
535. 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] resolved_spec in state is not decodable: %w; %s", err, recoveryCorruptSnapshot)
536. 		}
537. 		return &d, nil
538. 	}
539. 	// Back-compat: state persisted before resolved_spec existed. Inline spec is
540. 	// still faithful verbatim.
541. 	if !state.Spec.IsNull() && state.Spec.ValueString() != "" {
542. 		if d, _, err := r.resolveSpec(ctx, state); err == nil {
543. 			return d, nil
544. 		}
545. 		return nil, nil
546. 	}
547. 	// Legacy spec_file state (no resolved_spec): re-reading the file at Update time
548. 	// yields the CURRENT (possibly already-changed) contents, and only deployed_version
549. 	// is recorded — that is NOT the actual prior configuration. Fabricating a prior from
550. 	// it (desired config + old version) would make a changed post_install look unchanged,
551. 	// make rollback restore the DESIRED settings, and health-check against the new spec —
552. 	// a false promise of transactional restoration. So we decline (nil); ModifyPlan
553. 	// instead forces a truthful replacement when the spec has actually changed.
554. 	return nil, nil
555. }

557. // stateSpec returns the deployment that Read and Delete must operate on: the ACTUAL
558. // deployed identity captured in the PERSISTED resolved_spec snapshot, never a fresh
559. // re-read of a mutable spec_file. Re-reading spec_file in these lifecycle operations is
560. // unsafe — an edit to an immutable field (target.hosts, service_name, install_root)
561. // would make Read query, and Delete destroy, the DESIRED target instead of the DEPLOYED
562. // one, removing state while orphaning the live service (Read) or destroying the wrong
563. // identity and leaving the original service installed (Delete).
564. //
565. // A non-empty resolved_spec that fails to decode is treated as STATE CORRUPTION and
566. // surfaced as an error — we must NOT silently fall back to the mutable spec_file, which
567. // could target the wrong identity. Legacy state written before resolved_spec existed has
568. // no snapshot: inline `spec` is faithful verbatim (verified==true), but a spec_file
569. // reread is NOT a trustworthy deployed identity (verified==false) so callers must not
570. // treat a missing manifest as resource absence.
571. func (r *DeploymentResource) stateSpec(ctx context.Context, state *deploymentModel) (d *spec.Deployment, hash string, verified bool, err error) {
572. 	if rs := state.ResolvedSpec.ValueString(); rs != "" {
573. 		var sd spec.Deployment
574. 		if uerr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(rs), &sd); uerr != nil {
575. 			return nil, "", false, fmt.Errorf("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] resolved_spec in state is not decodable: %w; %s", uerr, recoveryCorruptSnapshot)
576. 		}
577. 		return &sd, state.SpecHash.ValueString(), true, nil
578. 	}
579. 	// Legacy state with no snapshot. Inline `spec` is faithful verbatim; a spec_file
580. 	// reread is unverifiable as the deployed identity.
581. 	verified = !state.Spec.IsNull() && state.Spec.ValueString() != ""
582. 	sd, h, rerr := r.resolveSpec(ctx, state)
583. 	return sd, h, verified, rerr
584. }
585. 
586. func (r *DeploymentResource) apply(ctx context.Context, plan *deploymentModel,
587. 	prior *spec.Deployment, diags diagAppender, setState func(*deploymentModel)) {
588. 	d, hash, err := r.resolveSpec(ctx, plan)
589. 	if err != nil {
590. 		diags.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_SPEC_INVALID", "invalid spec", err), err.Error())
591. 		return
592. 	}
593. 	eng := r.engine()
594. 	st, err := eng.Update(ctx, d, prior)
595. 	for _, w := range eng.Warns() {
596. 		diags.AddWarning(warnSummary(w), w)
597. 	}
598. 	if err != nil {
599. 		diags.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_CONNECT", "deploy failed", err), err.Error())
600. 		return
601. 	}
602. 	plan.ID = types.StringValue(deploymentID(d))
603. 	plan.Name = types.StringValue(d.Metadata.Name)
604. 	plan.SpecHash = types.StringValue(hash)
605. 	plan.ResolvedSpec = marshalResolvedSpec(d)
606. 	fillStatus(ctx, plan, st, diags)
607. 	setState(plan)
608. }

610. func (r *DeploymentResource) Read(ctx context.Context, req resource.ReadRequest, resp *resource.ReadResponse) {
611. 	var state deploymentModel
612. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &state)...)
613. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
614. 		return
615. 	}
616. 	d, _, verified, err := r.stateSpec(ctx, &state)
617. 	if err != nil {
618. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_SPEC_INVALID", "invalid spec in state", err), err.Error())
619. 		return
620. 	}
621. 	eng := r.engine()
622. 	st, err := eng.ReadStatus(ctx, d)
623. 	for _, w := range eng.Warns() {
624. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddWarning(warnSummary(w), w)
625. 	}
626. 	if err != nil {
627. 		// DESIGN §10.4: refresh MUST fail loudly on transport errors (no silent
628. 		// drop). We surface an ERROR diagnostic but do NOT RemoveResource, so the
629. 		// prior state is retained — an unreachable target is not a deleted
630. 		// resource (evaluator item 4).
631. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_CONNECT", "read failed", err), err.Error())
632. 		return
633. 	}
634. 	if st == nil { // manifest absent
635. 		if !verified {
636. 			// Unverifiable legacy spec_file target: we queried a spec_file re-read, not a
637. 			// persisted snapshot, so a missing manifest may only mean the file was edited to
638. 			// point at a DIFFERENT target — treating it as absence would drop state and
639. 			// orphan the still-deployed service. Retain state and demand an explicit
640. 			// migration instead of silently removing the resource.
641. 			resp.Diagnostics.AddError("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] labdeploy state migration required",
642. 				"a missing manifest here may be the result of a spec_file edit pointing at a "+
643. 					"different target rather than a real deletion, so removing state would orphan the "+
644. 					"still-deployed service. "+recoveryUnverifiableLegacy)
645. 			return
646. 		}
647. 		resp.State.RemoveResource(ctx) // verified snapshot ⇒ genuine absence
648. 		return
649. 	}
650. 	state.Name = types.StringValue(d.Metadata.Name)
651. 	fillStatus(ctx, &state, st, &resp.Diagnostics)
652. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, &state)...)
653. }

655. func (r *DeploymentResource) Delete(ctx context.Context, req resource.DeleteRequest, resp *resource.DeleteResponse) {
656. 	var state deploymentModel
657. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &state)...)
658. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
659. 		return
660. 	}
661. 	deleteTimeout, diags := state.Timeouts.Delete(ctx, defaultDeleteTimeout)
662. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(diags...)
663. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
664. 		return
665. 	}
666. 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, deleteTimeout)
667. 	defer cancel()
668. 	d, _, verified, err := r.stateSpec(ctx, &state)
669. 	if err != nil {
670. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_SPEC_INVALID", "invalid spec in state", err), err.Error())
671. 		return
672. 	}
673. 	if !verified {
674. 		// Legacy spec_file state with no persisted resolved_spec snapshot: the identity
675. 		// we would destroy comes from a fresh spec_file reread, NOT the deployed snapshot.
676. 		// An immutable-field edit on disk (host, service_name, install_root) would make
677. 		// Destroy target the WRONG service and orphan the one actually deployed. Refuse to
678. 		// destroy an unverifiable identity; demand an explicit migration first.
679. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddError("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] labdeploy state migration required",
680. 			"the identity to destroy cannot be verified from state — it would be re-derived from "+
681. 				"the current spec_file, which may have been edited to point at a different target, so "+
682. 				"destroying now could orphan the deployed service. "+recoveryUnverifiableLegacy)
683. 		return
684. 	}
685. 	eng := r.engine()
686. 	if err := eng.Destroy(ctx, d, state.DestroyMode.ValueString()); err != nil {
687. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_CONNECT", "destroy failed", err), err.Error())
688. 		return
689. 	}
690. 	for _, w := range eng.Warns() {
691. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddWarning(warnSummary(w), w)
692. 	}
693. }

695. // ImportState is unsupported in v1 (DESIGN §5.2): manifests carry target truth
696. // but TF state needs the spec input, which import cannot reconstruct. The message
697. // is the pinned string from DESIGN §5.2.
698. func (r *DeploymentResource) ImportState(ctx context.Context, req resource.ImportStateRequest, resp *resource.ImportStateResponse) {
699. 	resp.Diagnostics.AddError("[ERR_UNSUPPORTED] import is not supported; adopt via apply",
700. 		"import is not supported; adopt via apply")

703. // ------------------------------ shared helpers ------------------------------
704. 
705. // diagSummary formats a diagnostic Summary per DESIGN §12: exactly
706. // "[<CODE>] <short>", using only codes from the closed §12 taxonomy table.
707. //
708. // Timeout taxonomy (DESIGN §8.1 vs §12): ERR_TIMEOUT is reserved for the OUTER
709. // Terraform resource-operation deadline (the create/update/delete timeouts block,
710. // or runner.timeout_seconds) expiring; a dial/transport/WinRM CHILD deadline that
711. // fires while the outer operation context is still live is a connectivity failure
712. // and MUST stay ERR_CONNECT. We therefore classify on the OPERATION CONTEXT ITSELF
713. // (ctx.Err() == context.DeadlineExceeded at the CRUD boundary) rather than on
714. // errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) — the latter would wrongly reclassify a
715. // nested transport deadline (which the engine surfaces as ERR_CONNECT) as a TF
716. // timeout even when the resource context has not expired.
717. //
718. // When the outer context is live, an *engine.CodedError surfaces its taxonomy code
719. // (e.g. ERR_CONNECT); otherwise the operation-appropriate fallback so the contract
720. // also holds for pre-flight (spec/state) errors that never reached the engine.
721. func diagSummary(ctx context.Context, fallback, short string, err error) string {
722. 	code := fallback
723. 	switch {
724. 	case ctx != nil && ctx.Err() == context.DeadlineExceeded:
725. 		code = "ERR_TIMEOUT"
726. 	default:
727. 		var ce *engine.CodedError
728. 		if errors.As(err, &ce) && ce.Code != "" {
729. 			code = ce.Code
730. 		}
731. 	}
732. 	return fmt.Sprintf("[%s] %s", code, short)
733. }
734. 
735. // warnSummary formats a warning Summary per DESIGN §12. Engine warnings are
736. // free-form and carry no taxonomy code, so they default to the stable WARN code;
737. // a warning that already embeds a bracketed code (e.g. "[ERR_ROLLBACK_FAILED]
738. // ...") surfaces that code.
739. func warnSummary(w string) string {
740. 	if strings.HasPrefix(w, "[") {
741. 		if i := strings.Index(w, "]"); i > 1 {
742. 			return fmt.Sprintf("[%s] labdeploy warning", w[1:i])
743. 		}
744. 	}
745. 	return "[WARN] labdeploy warning"
746. }
747. 
748. type diagAppender = interface {
749. 	AddError(summary, detail string)
750. 	AddWarning(summary, detail string)
751. }
752. 
753. // deploymentID computes the stable, host-order- AND host-case-independent resource
754. // id (DESIGN §5.2 / architecture.md line 78): sha1(sorted(lower(hosts))+"/"+name)
755. // [0:12] + ":" + name. Hosts are lower-cased and sorted before hashing — matching
756. // immutableKey and the case-insensitive host semantics of DESIGN §9.5 — so the id is
757. // byte-identical when the same hosts are supplied in a different order OR a different
758. // case. This alignment is load-bearing: immutableKey treats a case-only host edit
759. // (e.g. "LAB-01" → "lab-01") as an in-place Update, not a replacement, so were the id
760. // case-sensitive that Update would recompute plan.ID to a new value while the id
761. // attribute's UseStateForUnknown modifier carried the old value forward, tripping
762. // Terraform's "Provider produced inconsistent result after apply" guard.
763. func deploymentID(d *spec.Deployment) string {
764. 	hosts := make([]string, len(d.Target.Hosts))
765. 	for i, h := range d.Target.Hosts {
766. 		hosts[i] = strings.ToLower(h)
767. 	}
768. 	sort.Strings(hosts)
769. 	sum := sha1.Sum([]byte(strings.Join(hosts, ",") + "/" + d.Metadata.Name))
770. 	return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])[:12] + ":" + d.Metadata.Name
771. }
772. 
773. func fillStatus(ctx context.Context, m *deploymentModel, st *engine.Status, diags diagAppender) {
774. 	m.DeployedVersion = types.StringValue(st.DeployedVersion)
775. 	m.PreviousVersion = types.StringValue(st.PreviousVersion)
776. 	m.ReleasePath = types.StringValue(st.ReleasePath)
777. 	m.ServiceStatus = types.StringValue(st.ServiceStatus)
778. 	hosts, d := types.ListValueFrom(ctx, types.StringType, st.Hosts)
779. 	if d.HasError() {
780. 		diags.AddError("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] internal error", fmt.Sprintf("hosts conversion: %v", d.Errors()))
781. 		return
782. 	}
783. 	m.Hosts = hosts
784. }

111. // deploymentSchema builds the resource schema at the given version. The attribute
112. // shape is identical across versions — only Version differs — so the same builder
113. // serves both the current Schema (v1) and the UpgradeState PriorSchema (v0). The v0→v1
114. // bump exists solely to trigger the state upgrader that backfills resolved_spec for
115. // legacy state persisted before the snapshot was populated.
116. func deploymentSchema(ctx context.Context, version int64) schema.Schema {
117. 	return schema.Schema{
118. 		Version:             version,
119. 		MarkdownDescription: "One application deployed to one host or one WSFC cluster (DESIGN §5.2).",
120. 		Attributes: map[string]schema.Attribute{
121. 			"spec":      schema.StringAttribute{Optional: true, MarkdownDescription: "Inline YAML/JSON Deployment spec. Exactly one of spec/spec_file."},
122. 			"spec_file": schema.StringAttribute{Optional: true, MarkdownDescription: "Path to a YAML/JSON Deployment spec on the runner."},
123. 			"variables": schema.MapAttribute{Optional: true, ElementType: types.StringType,
124. 				MarkdownDescription: "Values for ${var:NAME} substitution (DESIGN §6.6)."},
125. 			"version_override": schema.StringAttribute{Optional: true,
126. 				MarkdownDescription: "Overrides artifact.version after substitution — the pipeline's rollout/rollback lever."},
127. 			"destroy_mode": schema.StringAttribute{Optional: true, Computed: true,
128. 				Default:             stringdefault.StaticString("purge"),
129. 				MarkdownDescription: "purge | unregister | abandon (DESIGN §10.6)."},
130. 			"id": schema.StringAttribute{Computed: true, PlanModifiers: []planmodifier.String{stringplanmodifier.UseStateForUnknown()}},
131. 			"name": schema.StringAttribute{Computed: true, PlanModifiers: []planmodifier.String{stringplanmodifier.UseStateForUnknown()},
132. 				MarkdownDescription: "Deployment name, from spec metadata.name (DESIGN §5.2). Immutable, so it uses the prior state value across in-place updates."},
133. 			"spec_hash": schema.StringAttribute{Computed: true},
134. 			"resolved_spec": schema.StringAttribute{Computed: true, Sensitive: true,
135. 				MarkdownDescription: "Internal: the fully-resolved deployment spec (post-substitution/version_override) as of the last apply, persisted so an Update can faithfully compare against the prior artifact and configuration even when spec_file contents have since changed on the runner. Marked sensitive because ${var:...} substitutions may embed secret values into the resolved spec."},
136. 			"deployed_version": schema.StringAttribute{Computed: true},
137. 			"previous_version": schema.StringAttribute{Computed: true},
138. 			"hosts":            schema.ListAttribute{Computed: true, ElementType: types.StringType},
139. 			"release_path":     schema.StringAttribute{Computed: true},
140. 			"service_status":   schema.StringAttribute{Computed: true},
141. 		},
142. 		Blocks: map[string]schema.Block{
143. 			// DESIGN §5.2: create/update default 30m, delete 15m. The block only
144. 			// declares the attributes; the defaults are applied at read time via
145. 			// Timeouts.Create/Update/Delete(ctx, default) in the CRUD methods.
146. 			"timeouts": timeouts.Block(ctx, timeouts.Opts{
147. 				Create: true,
148. 				Update: true,
149. 				Delete: true,
150. 			}),
151. 		},
152. 	}

155. // UpgradeState migrates state persisted at an earlier schema version. The v0→v1
156. // upgrader BACKFILLS resolved_spec for legacy state written before the snapshot
157. // attribute was populated, converting an unverifiable spec_file deployment into a
158. // VERIFIED snapshot BEFORE any plan/refresh acts on it. This is the migration path
159. // that breaks the legacy deadlock (ModifyPlan forcing replacement ↔ Delete refusing
160. // snapshot-less state) WITHOUT any unsafe deletion.
161. //
162. // The backfill is TRUSTWORTHY ONLY when the current spec_file still resolves to the
163. // SAME spec_hash that was persisted at the last apply — i.e. the file has NOT been
164. // edited since the deployment. If the operator upgraded the provider AND edited the
165. // spec in the same step, the file now describes the DESIRED (not deployed) config, so
166. // snapshotting it would fabricate a false prior — suppressing immutable replacement,
167. // reconfiguration, changed post_install, and truthful rollback. In that case (or when
168. // no baseline spec_hash exists, or the spec cannot be resolved) we DECLINE to backfill,
169. // leave resolved_spec empty, warn, and let the downstream Read/Delete guards +
170. // legacyReplaceRequired safeguard keep the state fail-safe.
171. func (r *DeploymentResource) UpgradeState(ctx context.Context) map[int64]resource.StateUpgrader {
172. 	priorSchema := deploymentSchema(ctx, 0)
173. 	return map[int64]resource.StateUpgrader{
174. 		0: {
175. 			PriorSchema: &priorSchema,
176. 			StateUpgrader: func(ctx context.Context, req resource.UpgradeStateRequest, resp *resource.UpgradeStateResponse) {
177. 				var state deploymentModel
178. 				resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &state)...)
179. 				if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
180. 					return
181. 				}
182. 				if state.ResolvedSpec.IsNull() || state.ResolvedSpec.ValueString() == "" {
183. 					r.backfillResolvedSpec(ctx, &state, &resp.Diagnostics)
184. 				}
185. 				resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, &state)...)
186. 			},
187. 		},
188. 	}
189. }

191. // backfillResolvedSpec reconstructs the resolved_spec snapshot for legacy state, but
192. // ONLY when the current spec resolves to the persisted spec_hash (proving the source
193. // is unchanged since deployment, so the snapshot faithfully captures the DEPLOYED
194. // identity). A missing baseline hash, a hash mismatch (source edited), a resolve
195. // error, or a provider default_target that contributes merged fields the pre-merge
196. // hash never covered all cause it to DECLINE and warn — never fabricate a prior.
197. func (r *DeploymentResource) backfillResolvedSpec(ctx context.Context, state *deploymentModel, diags *diag.Diagnostics) {
198. 	d, hash, defaultsContributed, err := r.resolveSpecDetail(ctx, state)
199. 	if err != nil {
200. 		diags.AddWarning("[WARN] labdeploy state not fully migrated",
201. 			"could not reconstruct a resolved_spec snapshot for this legacy resource "+
202. 				"(the spec could not be resolved: "+err.Error()+"). Lifecycle operations "+
203. 				"remain fail-safe; run terraform apply once the spec is resolvable to persist "+
204. 				"the snapshot.")
205. 		return
206. 	}
207. 	persisted := state.SpecHash.ValueString()
208. 	if persisted == "" || persisted != hash {
209. 		// The source no longer matches what was deployed (edited alongside the provider
210. 		// upgrade) or there is no baseline to compare. Snapshotting now would record the
211. 		// DESIRED config as the deployed prior — a false, high-impact fabrication. Decline.
212. 		diags.AddWarning("[WARN] labdeploy state not fully migrated",
213. 			"the current spec no longer matches the spec_hash recorded at the last apply "+
214. 				"(or no baseline spec_hash exists), so a resolved_spec snapshot cannot be "+
215. 				"trusted to reflect the DEPLOYED configuration. Leaving the snapshot unset so "+
216. 				"immutable-field replacement, reconfiguration, and rollback stay truthful; "+
217. 				"re-apply against the currently deployed spec to persist a faithful snapshot.")
218. 		return
219. 	}
220. 	if defaultsContributed {
221. 		// spec_hash matches because it is computed over the RAW spec, BEFORE provider
222. 		// default_target is merged. A default_target that now contributes target fields
223. 		// (transport/os/port/credentials/winrm) means the resolved_spec identity depends
224. 		// on provider config the persisted hash never covered — the merged fields may
225. 		// never have been deployed. Decline so a provider-default change cannot fabricate
226. 		// the deployed identity during state migration.
227. 		diags.AddWarning("[WARN] labdeploy state not fully migrated",
228. 			"the current spec relies on provider default_target values to fill one or more "+
229. 				"target fields, but spec_hash is computed before those defaults are merged, "+
230. 				"so it cannot prove the merged configuration was ever deployed. Leaving the "+
231. 				"resolved_spec snapshot unset so immutable-field replacement, reconfiguration, "+
232. 				"and rollback stay truthful; re-apply against the currently deployed spec to "+
233. 				"persist a faithful snapshot.")
234. 		return
235. 	}
236. 	state.ResolvedSpec = marshalResolvedSpec(d)
237. }

246. // resolveSpec loads+parses the deployment for a model (DESIGN §6.1).
247. func (r *DeploymentResource) resolveSpec(ctx context.Context, m *deploymentModel) (*spec.Deployment, string, error) {
248. 	d, hash, _, err := r.resolveSpecDetail(ctx, m)
249. 	return d, hash, err
250. }
251. 
252. // resolveSpecDetail is resolveSpec plus a defaultsContributed flag reporting whether
253. // the provider's default_target actually filled any target field during the merge.
254. // spec_hash is computed over the RAW (pre-merge) spec, so it CANNOT detect a change to
255. // provider default_target: an unchanged spec_file hashes identically even when a new
256. // default now contributes never-deployed fields to the resolved spec. The flag lets the
257. // state-migration backfill refuse to snapshot a resolved_spec whose identity depends on
258. // provider config that the persisted hash never covered.
259. func (r *DeploymentResource) resolveSpecDetail(ctx context.Context, m *deploymentModel) (*spec.Deployment, string, bool, error) {
260. 	hasSpec := !m.Spec.IsNull() && m.Spec.ValueString() != ""
261. 	hasFile := !m.SpecFile.IsNull() && m.SpecFile.ValueString() != ""
262. 	if hasSpec == hasFile {
263. 		return nil, "", false, fmt.Errorf("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] exactly one of spec/spec_file must be set")
264. 	}
265. 	raw := m.Spec.ValueString()
266. 	if hasFile {
267. 		b, err := os.ReadFile(m.SpecFile.ValueString())
268. 		if err != nil {
269. 			return nil, "", false, fmt.Errorf("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] spec_file: %w", err)
270. 		}
271. 		raw = string(b)
272. 	}
273. 	vars := map[string]string{}
274. 	if !m.Variables.IsNull() {
275. 		if diag := m.Variables.ElementsAs(ctx, &vars, false); diag.HasError() {
276. 			return nil, "", false, fmt.Errorf("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] variables: %v", diag.Errors())
277. 		}
278. 	}
279. 	d, hash, err := spec.ParseDeploymentLenient(raw, vars, m.VersionOverride.ValueString())
280. 	if err != nil {
281. 		return nil, "", false, err // already [ERR_SPEC_INVALID]-coded by the spec package
282. 	}
283. 	defaultsContributed := false
284. 	if r.pd != nil && r.pd.DefaultTarget != nil {
285. 		before := d.Target
286. 		spec.MergeTargetDefaults(&d.Target, r.pd.DefaultTarget)
287. 		defaultsContributed = !reflect.DeepEqual(before, d.Target)
288. 	}
289. 	if err := spec.ValidateDeployment(d); err != nil { // validate post-merge (DESIGN §6.2)
290. 		return nil, "", false, err // already [ERR_SPEC_INVALID]-coded
291. 	}
292. 	return d, hash, defaultsContributed, nil
293. }

295. // immutableKey captures the spec paths that force replacement (DESIGN §5.2):
296. // pattern.type, service_name, role_name, install_root, metadata.name,
297. // target.hosts, target.os. target.hosts is compared as a SET (lower-cased and
298. // sorted) per architecture.md line 350: reordering the same hosts is NOT a
299. // replacement, only adding/removing a host is.
300. func immutableKey(d *spec.Deployment) string {
301. 	hosts := make([]string, len(d.Target.Hosts))
302. 	for i, h := range d.Target.Hosts {
303. 		hosts[i] = strings.ToLower(h)
304. 	}
305. 	sort.Strings(hosts)
306. 	return strings.Join([]string{
307. 		string(d.Pattern.Type), d.Pattern.ServiceName, d.Pattern.RoleName,
308. 		d.Pattern.EffectiveInstallRoot(d.Target.OS), d.Metadata.Name,
309. 		strings.Join(hosts, ","), string(d.Target.OS),
310. 	}, "|")
311. }

313. // Recovery procedures surfaced in migration/corruption diagnostics. These are
314. // EXECUTABLE and reach VERIFIED state without the dead-ends the guards block: neither
315. // `terraform apply -replace` (whose Delete half is refused for unverifiable/corrupt
316. // state) nor "pin the defaulted fields then apply" (which changes the pre-merge hash and
317. // so forces the same blocked replacement). The escape hatch is `terraform state rm`
318. // followed by `terraform apply`: state rm is a state-only operation (it never touches the
319. // live service or invokes Delete), and the subsequent apply recreates the resource via
320. // Create, which deploys IDEMPOTENTLY (adopting the already-running service when the spec
321. // matches it) and persists a verified resolved_spec snapshot. ModifyPlan's create branch
322. // returns before the update guards, so this path is never blocked.
323. const (
324. 	// recoveryUnverifiableDefaults applies when the deployed identity cannot be verified
325. 	// from state AND provider default_target contributes immutable fields the pre-merge
326. 	// spec_hash does not cover.
327. 	recoveryUnverifiableDefaults = "the deployed identity cannot be verified from state and " +
328. 		"the provider default_target contributes one or more target fields (transport/os/port/" +
329. 		"hosts/credentials/winrm) that spec_hash — computed before defaults are merged — does not " +
330. 		"cover, so planning an update could deploy to a newly-defaulted target and orphan the " +
331. 		"original deployment. Recovery: first make this spec (or default_target) describe the " +
332. 		"ACTUALLY deployed identity, then run `terraform state rm <address>` followed by " +
333. 		"`terraform apply`. state rm is state-only (it never destroys the live service or invokes " +
334. 		"the guarded Delete); the apply then recreates via Create, which deploys idempotently " +
335. 		"(adopting the existing service when the spec matches) and persists a verified resolved_spec " +
336. 		"snapshot. Do NOT instead pin the defaults and re-apply in place: that changes the pre-merge " +
337. 		"hash and forces a replacement whose Delete half is refused for this unverifiable state."
338. 
339. 	// recoveryUnverifiableLegacy applies to legacy spec_file state with no snapshot and no
340. 	// contributing defaults.
341. 	recoveryUnverifiableLegacy = "this resource predates resolved_spec and is configured via " +
342. 		"spec_file, so its deployed identity cannot be verified from state. Recovery: run " +
343. 		"`terraform apply` WITHOUT editing the spec_file — with no immutable change pending, planning " +
344. 		"does not force a replacement, so the apply flows through Update and persists a resolved_spec " +
345. 		"snapshot from the currently-deployed spec. If planning instead forces a replacement (e.g. the " +
346. 		"spec must change), run `terraform state rm <address>` then `terraform apply` to re-adopt via a " +
347. 		"fresh Create. Both reach verified state without the guarded Delete destroying an unverifiable " +
348. 		"identity. (Do NOT use `terraform apply -replace` — its destroy half is blocked for exactly " +
349. 		"this reason.)"
350. 
351. 	// recoveryCorruptSnapshot applies when a non-empty resolved_spec cannot be decoded. It
352. 	// cannot be repaired in place; the state entry must be removed so the resource can be
353. 	// re-adopted against the live service.
354. 	recoveryCorruptSnapshot = "the persisted resolved_spec snapshot is corrupt and cannot be " +
355. 		"decoded, so the deployed identity is unknown; the Read/Delete guards refuse to act on it to " +
356. 		"avoid querying or destroying the wrong identity. Recovery: run `terraform state rm <address>` " +
357. 		"then `terraform apply` to re-adopt via a fresh Create (which deploys idempotently and persists " +
358. 		"a verified snapshot), or restore a known-good state backup — the corrupt snapshot cannot be " +
359. 		"repaired in place, and state rm never invokes the guarded Delete."
360. )

362. // ModifyPlan computes spec_hash drift and RequiresReplace on immutable paths.
363. func (r *DeploymentResource) ModifyPlan(ctx context.Context, req resource.ModifyPlanRequest, resp *resource.ModifyPlanResponse) {
364. 	if req.Plan.Raw.IsNull() { // destroy
365. 		return
366. 	}
367. 	var plan deploymentModel
368. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.Plan.Get(ctx, &plan)...)
369. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
370. 		return
371. 	}
372. 	newSpec, newHash, defaultsContributed, err := r.resolveSpecDetail(ctx, &plan)
373. 	if err != nil {
374. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_SPEC_INVALID", "invalid spec", err), err.Error())
375. 		return
376. 	}
377. 	plan.SpecHash = types.StringValue(newHash)
378. 	// Persist the fully-resolved spec at plan time so it is known (no perpetual
379. 	// "known after apply" diff) and so a later Update can compare against it even
380. 	// after spec_file contents change on disk.
381. 	plan.ResolvedSpec = marshalResolvedSpec(newSpec)
382. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.Plan.Set(ctx, &plan)...)
383. 
384. 	if req.State.Raw.IsNull() { // create
385. 		return
386. 	}
387. 	var state deploymentModel
388. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &state)...)
389. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
390. 		return
391. 	}
392. 	// Compare against the PERSISTED prior spec, not a fresh re-read of spec_file
393. 	// (which by plan time already holds the NEW contents and would make old == new,
394. 	// hiding immutable-field changes).
395. 	oldSpec, perr := r.priorFromState(ctx, &state)
396. 	if perr != nil {
397. 		// Corrupt persisted snapshot: fail loudly (consistent with stateSpec) rather than
398. 		// planning an update against an untrustworthy prior that could target the wrong host.
399. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_SPEC_INVALID", "invalid spec in state", perr), perr.Error())
400. 		return
401. 	}
402. 	if oldSpec == nil {
403. 		// No faithful prior snapshot. When provider default_target contributes fields to the
404. 		// resolved spec, spec_hash (computed pre-merge) cannot detect a default change, and
405. 		// because that hash is unchanged we CANNOT hang a replacement off spec_hash. Adopting
406. 		// the merged spec would silently deploy to the newly-defaulted target and orphan the
407. 		// original deployment. BLOCK the plan with an executable recovery instead of laundering
408. 		// the unverifiable merged identity into state.
409. 		if defaultsContributed {
410. 			resp.Diagnostics.AddError("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] labdeploy state migration required", recoveryUnverifiableDefaults)
411. 			return
412. 		}
413. 		// Otherwise the v0→v1 state upgrader normally backfilled resolved_spec already; this
414. 		// branch is only reached when even the upgrader could not reconstruct a snapshot. We
415. 		// cannot honestly Reconfigure without the ACTUAL prior configuration, so when the
416. 		// resolved spec really changed (hash drift), force a REPLACEMENT to apply the change via
417. 		// a full, truthful create/deploy. No drift ⇒ nothing to do.
418. 		if legacyReplaceRequired(oldSpec, newHash, &state) {
419. 			resp.RequiresReplace = append(resp.RequiresReplace, path.Root("spec_hash"))
420. 		}
421. 		return
422. 	}
423. 	if immutableKey(oldSpec) != immutableKey(newSpec) {
424. 		resp.RequiresReplace = append(resp.RequiresReplace, configuredSpecPath(&plan))
425. 	}
426. }
427. 
428. // legacyReplaceRequired reports whether an update must be handled as a truthful
429. // REPLACEMENT because no faithful prior snapshot exists to reconfigure against.
430. // oldSpec==nil means priorFromState could not reconstruct a trustworthy prior
431. // (legacy spec_file state written before resolved_spec); newHash != the persisted
432. // spec_hash means the resolved spec really changed. When both hold, forcing a
433. // replacement is safer than feeding fabricated prior state to Reconfigure. No drift
434. // ⇒ no change to apply, so no replacement.
435. func legacyReplaceRequired(oldSpec *spec.Deployment, newHash string, state *deploymentModel) bool {
436. 	return oldSpec == nil && newHash != state.SpecHash.ValueString()
437. }
438. 
439. // configuredSpecPath returns the schema path of whichever spec attribute the
440. // configuration actually sets, so a forced replacement is attributed to spec_file
441. // when that is the source rather than always to spec.
442. func configuredSpecPath(m *deploymentModel) path.Path {
443. 	if !m.SpecFile.IsNull() && m.SpecFile.ValueString() != "" {
444. 		return path.Root("spec_file")
445. 	}
446. 	return path.Root("spec")
447. }

449. // marshalResolvedSpec serializes a resolved deployment to canonical JSON for
450. // persistence in the resolved_spec computed attribute. password_env and other
451. // secret references are stored by NAME, but ${var:...} substitutions may embed
452. // secret values into other fields, so the snapshot can contain sensitive data —
453. // it is persisted only in the Sensitive resolved_spec attribute. Returns null on
454. // the (practically impossible) marshal error.
455. func marshalResolvedSpec(d *spec.Deployment) types.String {
456. 	b, err := json.Marshal(d)
457. 	if err != nil {
458. 		return types.StringNull()
459. 	}
460. 	return types.StringValue(string(b))
461. }

481. func (r *DeploymentResource) Update(ctx context.Context, req resource.UpdateRequest, resp *resource.UpdateResponse) {
482. 	var plan deploymentModel
483. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.Plan.Get(ctx, &plan)...)
484. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
485. 		return
486. 	}
487. 	updateTimeout, diags := plan.Timeouts.Update(ctx, defaultUpdateTimeout)
488. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(diags...)
489. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
490. 		return
491. 	}
492. 	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, updateTimeout)
493. 	defer cancel()
494. 	// Resolve the PRIOR spec from state so a same-artifact configuration change is
495. 	// routed through the transactional Reconfigure path instead of Deploy, whose
496. 	// idempotency short-circuit would otherwise skip it. Decoding errors are NOT
497. 	// swallowed — corrupt/incompatible state must surface rather than silently
498. 	// downgrade to a blind Deploy.
499. 	var state deploymentModel
500. 	resp.Diagnostics.Append(req.State.Get(ctx, &state)...)
501. 	if resp.Diagnostics.HasError() {
502. 		return
503. 	}
504. 	prior, perr := r.priorFromState(ctx, &state)
505. 	if perr != nil {
506. 		// Corrupt persisted snapshot: surface it (consistent with stateSpec / ModifyPlan)
507. 		// rather than feeding a fabricated or nil prior into a blind Deploy.
508. 		resp.Diagnostics.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_SPEC_INVALID", "invalid spec in state", perr), perr.Error())
509. 		return
510. 	}
511. 	r.apply(ctx, &plan, prior, &resp.Diagnostics, func(m *deploymentModel) {
512. 		resp.Diagnostics.Append(resp.State.Set(ctx, m)...)
513. 	})
514. }

516. // priorFromState reconstructs the prior deployment from the PERSISTED resolved_spec
517. // (written verbatim on the last apply/plan), so it is faithful regardless of whether
518. // the prior spec came from inline `spec` or from a `spec_file` whose contents have
519. // since changed on the runner. This is what lets a same-artifact spec_file
520. // configuration change route correctly through Reconfigure (applying CONFIGURE and a
521. // changed post_install) while a real artifact upgrade still routes to Deploy, and it
522. // gives rollback the ACTUAL prior configuration to restore. A non-empty resolved_spec
523. // that fails to decode is STATE CORRUPTION: it returns an error (consistent with
524. // stateSpec) so Update/ModifyPlan fail loudly instead of fabricating a prior. Falls back
525. // to re-parsing inline spec for state written before resolved_spec existed (still faithful
526. // verbatim); returns (nil, nil) for legacy spec_file state (whose on-disk contents cannot
527. // be trusted as the prior) so ModifyPlan can force a truthful replacement.
528. func (r *DeploymentResource) priorFromState(ctx context.Context, state *deploymentModel) (*spec.Deployment, error) {
529. 	if rs := state.ResolvedSpec.ValueString(); rs != "" {
530. 		var d spec.Deployment
531. 		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(rs), &d); err != nil {
532. 			// Corrupt snapshot: do NOT fall back to the mutable spec_file (which could target
533. 			// the wrong identity) and do NOT return a nil "no prior" (which Update would treat
534. 			// as a blind first deploy). Surface it as state corruption.
535. 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] resolved_spec in state is not decodable: %w; %s", err, recoveryCorruptSnapshot)
536. 		}
537. 		return &d, nil
538. 	}
539. 	// Back-compat: state persisted before resolved_spec existed. Inline spec is
540. 	// still faithful verbatim.
541. 	if !state.Spec.IsNull() && state.Spec.ValueString() != "" {
542. 		if d, _, err := r.resolveSpec(ctx, state); err == nil {
543. 			return d, nil
544. 		}
545. 		return nil, nil
546. 	}
547. 	// Legacy spec_file state (no resolved_spec): re-reading the file at Update time
548. 	// yields the CURRENT (possibly already-changed) contents, and only deployed_version
549. 	// is recorded — that is NOT the actual prior configuration. Fabricating a prior from
550. 	// it (desired config + old version) would make a changed post_install look unchanged,
551. 	// make rollback restore the DESIRED settings, and health-check against the new spec —
552. 	// a false promise of transactional restoration. So we decline (nil); ModifyPlan
553. 	// instead forces a truthful replacement when the spec has actually changed.
554. 	return nil, nil
555. }
556. 
557. // stateSpec returns the deployment that Read and Delete must operate on: the ACTUAL
558. // deployed identity captured in the PERSISTED resolved_spec snapshot, never a fresh
559. // re-read of a mutable spec_file. Re-reading spec_file in these lifecycle operations is
560. // unsafe — an edit to an immutable field (target.hosts, service_name, install_root)
561. // would make Read query, and Delete destroy, the DESIRED target instead of the DEPLOYED
562. // one, removing state while orphaning the live service (Read) or destroying the wrong
563. // identity and leaving the original service installed (Delete).
564. //
565. // A non-empty resolved_spec that fails to decode is treated as STATE CORRUPTION and
566. // surfaced as an error — we must NOT silently fall back to the mutable spec_file, which
567. // could target the wrong identity. Legacy state written before resolved_spec existed has
568. // no snapshot: inline `spec` is faithful verbatim (verified==true), but a spec_file
569. // reread is NOT a trustworthy deployed identity (verified==false) so callers must not
570. // treat a missing manifest as resource absence.
571. func (r *DeploymentResource) stateSpec(ctx context.Context, state *deploymentModel) (d *spec.Deployment, hash string, verified bool, err error) {
572. 	if rs := state.ResolvedSpec.ValueString(); rs != "" {
573. 		var sd spec.Deployment
574. 		if uerr := json.Unmarshal([]byte(rs), &sd); uerr != nil {
575. 			return nil, "", false, fmt.Errorf("[ERR_SPEC_INVALID] resolved_spec in state is not decodable: %w; %s", uerr, recoveryCorruptSnapshot)
576. 		}
577. 		return &sd, state.SpecHash.ValueString(), true, nil
578. 	}
579. 	// Legacy state with no snapshot. Inline `spec` is faithful verbatim; a spec_file
580. 	// reread is unverifiable as the deployed identity.
581. 	verified = !state.Spec.IsNull() && state.Spec.ValueString() != ""
582. 	sd, h, rerr := r.resolveSpec(ctx, state)
583. 	return sd, h, verified, rerr
584. }

586. func (r *DeploymentResource) apply(ctx context.Context, plan *deploymentModel,
587. 	prior *spec.Deployment, diags diagAppender, setState func(*deploymentModel)) {
588. 	d, hash, err := r.resolveSpec(ctx, plan)
589. 	if err != nil {
590. 		diags.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_SPEC_INVALID", "invalid spec", err), err.Error())
591. 		return
592. 	}
593. 	eng := r.engine()
594. 	st, err := eng.Update(ctx, d, prior)
595. 	for _, w := range eng.Warns() {
596. 		diags.AddWarning(warnSummary(w), w)
597. 	}
598. 	if err != nil {
599. 		diags.AddError(diagSummary(ctx, "ERR_CONNECT", "deploy failed", err), err.Error())
600. 		return
601. 	}
602. 	plan.ID = types.StringValue(deploymentID(d))
603. 	plan.Name = types.StringValue(d.Metadata.Name)
604. 	plan.SpecHash = types.StringValue(hash)
605. 	plan.ResolvedSpec = marshalResolvedSpec(d)
606. 	fillStatus(ctx, plan, st, diags)
607. 	setState(plan)
608. }
